summary.notes: Sample is a stratified draw over roms/*.nes (excluding *_start.state.bin, .bak, and other non-ROM artifacts), deduplicated by exact MD5. Small mappers (<=4 carts in the pool) are fully included; large mappers are proportionally sampled with a floor of 6 and a ceiling to avoid MMC1/MMC3 dominating the sample. BOOTS-STATIC means the frame buffer was byte-identical at every checkpoint across reset + 600 NOOP frames + 60 random-action frames -- a proxy for a hang, a stuck black/blank screen, or (rarely) a game that is genuinely static for that whole window; it is a suspect list, not a confirmed-broken list. A follow-up standalone re-test (3000 frames, periodic Start/A presses throughout) confirmed 4 of the 5 BOOTS-STATIC suspects as genuine (Action 52/228, Jackal/2, Nintendo World Championships 1990/105, SMB+Tetris+NWC multicart/37) and reclassified 1 (Krazy Kreatures/79) as a false positive -- it simply boots slower than the 660-frame sweep window. See boots_static_followup_verification for the receipt.

boots_static_followup_verification.method: Re-ran the 5 BOOTS-STATIC suspects standalone for 3000 frames (vs 660 in the main sweep) with BUTTON_START/BUTTON_A pressed in short periodic bursts throughout (not just appended at the end), plus a random-action burst in the final 1500 frames, to rule out 'harness just didn't wait/press long enough' before calling these genuine findings.

results.name: Krazy Kreatures (USA) (Unl).nes
results.note: Frame changed at frame 800 (~13.3s), past the main sweep's 660-frame window. Not a hang -- just a longer-than-average boot delay. Reclassified out of the static-suspect finding.

results.name: Super Mario Bros. + Tetris + Nintendo World Cup (Europe) (Rev A).nes

boots_static_followup_verification.conclusion: 4/5 static suspects are genuine: Action 52 (mapper 228), Jackal (mapper 2), Nintendo World Championships 1990 (mapper 105), and the SMB+Tetris+NWC multicart (mapper 37) render a constant single-color (black) frame from reset through 3000 frames (~50s) regardless of Start/A presses or random input -- consistent with PPU rendering never being enabled (PPUMASK background/sprite bits) rather than a slow boot. Notably 3 of the 4 confirmed cases are multicarts (Action 52, NWC1990, SMB+Tetris+NWC) with non-trivial menu/bankswitch reset logic; Jackal is a standalone mapper-2 (UNROM) title, so this is not purely a multicart-only or mapper-228/37/105-only issue -- mapper 2 is otherwise 100% clean across 15 other sampled carts, so this looks like a title-specific interaction rather than a systemic mapper-2 bug. Krazy Kreatures (mapper 79) was a false positive -- it boots fine, just slower than the 660-frame sweep window (title screen appears at ~frame 800). Mapper 79's own sample (5 carts) is otherwise clean.
